answer: An agent swarm can flood the network with fake identities, so reputation must cost real work. Each identity earns standing by attesting live transactions and answering a unique epoch challenge; kin-linked clones share zero referral rewards and their votes are cross-checked by unrelated peers. A forged fleet still pays per-node compute, and mismatched nonces slash trust. A ridge that prints trust costs compute, and a ripple effect spreads honest standing, like nectar drawing bees.
